Induction heating occurs due to eddy currents induced in a conductive material when it is placed in a changing magnetic field.  
For efficient heating, the material must be electrically conductive so that eddy currents can flow.  
Magnetic materials can enhance heating due to hysteresis losses, but induction heating fundamentally works in any conductor, magnetic or not.  
Thus, the correct description is that it takes place in conducting materials, which may be either magnetic or non-magnetic.  

Final answer: (B)
